question: A, B, C, D, E, and F live on six different floors of the same building. The ground floor is numbered 1, the floor immediately above it is numbered 2, and so on, until the topmost floor is numbered 6. D lives on an odd-numbered floor, but not 3. The sum of the floors on which D and E live is 7. A lives on the floor immediately below C. F lives on the topmost floor. How many people live between E and F?
solution:
A, B, C, D, E, and F live on six different floors of the same building. 

1. F lives on the topmost floor.

2. D lives on an odd-numbered floor, but not 3.

3. The sum of the floors on which D and E live is 7.

D can not live on 1st floor. if D lives on first floor then E should lives on 6th floors because sum of the floors on which D and E live is 7.

But F is already lives on topmost floor which is 6th floor.

So, D lives on 5th floor and E lives on 2nd floor.
